# Mahākaccānabhaddekaratta Sutta (MN 133 (PTS MN iii 192))

**ID:** MN 133 (PTS MN iii 192)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Mahākaccānabhaddekaratta Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** Mahākaccāna and One Fine Night
**PTS:** MN iii 192
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahākaccānabhaddekaratta Sutta* (MN 133) is the 133rd discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya*, situated at Tapodārāma (the Hot Springs Park) near Rājagaha [Galasek 2016; Holz]. In the narrative setting, after the monk Samiddhi is questioned near dawn by a radiant deity concerning the summary and exposition of the "one who has had an auspicious night" (*bhaddekaratta*), Samiddhi approaches the Buddha to request this instruction [Caudron 2000; Galasek 2016; Holz]. The Buddha recites the enigmatic core verses—which emphasize abandoning longing for the past or anticipation of the future and striving energetically for present insight—and then departs into his dwelling without providing an explanation [Caudron 2000; Nyanaponika, Hecker, Bodhi 2003; Rogell 2003]. The monks subsequently turn to Venerable Mahākaccāna to furnish a full exposition (*vibhaṅga*) of the Buddha's brief summary (*uddesa*) [Buswell 2007; Caudron 2000; Holz]. While the Buddha explains the verses in terms of the five aggregates in MN 131, Mahākaccāna elucidates them through the cognitive operation of the internal and external sense bases (*saḷāyatana*) and the cessation of delight across the three temporal periods [Emmrich 2012; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995; Rogell 2003].

 The core of the Chinese *Bhadrakarātrī-sūtra* corresponds nearly word for word with MN 133 and MĀ 165 [Holz]. DharmaNexus independently confirms extensive cross-language alignments with MĀ 165 (ZH_T01_0026) and the Tibetan *Bhadrakarātrī* (D 313) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali Canon, DharmaNexus records major textual reuse with the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), the *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), and the *Madhupiṇḍika Sutta* (MN 18), as well as the other *Bhaddekaratta* texts (MN 131, MN 132, MN 134) [DharmaNexus].
